title: Glorification
definition: Glorification is the final completion of salvation when believers are fully conformed to Christ and freed from sin and death forever.
summary: Glorification is the promised completion of God's saving work in His people.
christFocus: The risen Christ will transform His people to be like Him and bring them into the fullness of eternal life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Glorification is the final stage of salvation. God will complete what He began. Believers who are justified and being sanctified will one day be fully transformed, free from sin, suffering, corruption, and death.

This hope is tied to the resurrection and return of Christ. When He appears, His people will be made like Him. Their bodies will be raised or transformed, and their fellowship with God will be unhindered.

Glorification gives hope in suffering and perseverance in weakness. The Christian life is moving toward a promised completion that cannot be lost by those who belong to Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many believers feel weary because they see remaining sin, pain, disability, grief, and weakness. Glorification matters because it promises that brokenness will not have the final word; Christ will finish His saving work.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Set your hope on the completion Christ has promised. Let future glory strengthen present endurance, holiness, worship, and courage in suffering.
